title: Sheaves of modules on a ringed space have enough injectives
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. The category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is abelian and has enough injectives: every $\mathcal O_X$-module admits a monomorphism into an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI (lemma-sheaves-modules-space), statement for an arbitrary ringed space

proof.text: Apply the Mathlib abelian instance [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-category-abelian] to the small category of opens of X with its open-cover topology and the underlying ring sheaf moduleRings X. This yields the first conjunct Nonempty (Abelian (Mod(O_X))).

Apply the proved upstream theorem SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Abelian to moduleRings X. Its small-site and equal-universe hypotheses hold for Opens X. Register the resulting Grothendieck structure as a local instance and apply [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] to obtain the second conjunct. Combine the two conjuncts. Neither the localized generator clause nor K-injective resolutions are used.

proof_origin.place: SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian specialized to moduleRings X; Mathlib SheafOfModules.instAbelian and IsGrothendieckAbelian.enoughInjectives. N1 second reading eliminates the open ringed-site Grothendieck and K-injective resolution dependencies.
